limitations: Final speech facts, actual backend effect completion, intentional interruption, capture readiness, and trace identity coverage are different outcomes; no aggregate overall quality-pass score is asserted.
A generated text/finished handle does not establish human intelligibility. Whole-stream ASR retains silence, acknowledgments and any interrupted old speech; the near-silent failure is not excluded.

Whitefield is explicitly present in all fifteen delivered Whitefield scenarios, but the ITPL suffix is consistently rendered differently by ASR. Literal spellings are preserved, not normalized into a posthoc proper-name whitelist.
The candidate clarification asks the correct initial question and truthfully reports a successful lookup after clarification, but never fulfills the original navigation action or ETA requirement.

Eleven trusted client/server trace equality failures remain recorded despite raw packet equality in all twenty-one cases; this semantic review does not promote identity-less packets or amend mechanical scores.

Synthetic independent development scenarios have fixed arm order, tiny per-condition counts and shared local hardware. This review does not establish physical playback latency, general accuracy or a causal model-speed benefit.
Exact reviewed transcript guards and source hashes bind labels to this run; they must not be silently reused with new transcripts. Model weights were not reread.
